annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence in Policing: AI technologies currently used to improve the efficiency and service delivery of police's corporate or enabling functions
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence in Policing: AI technologies currently used to improve the efficiency and service delivery of police's corporate or enabling functions
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Evidence Based Policing Centre, New Zealand Police
annotation.summary_en: New Zealand Police Evidence Based Policing Centre report reviewing AI tools (report drafting, redaction, transcription, video/biometric analysis, call translation, recruitment) used in Five Eyes policing for corporate functions. It identifies challenges (performance, governance, privacy, internal trust) and recommends human-in-the-loop, alignment with NZ Police frameworks and the Algorithm Charter.
key_provisions_or_claims: No specific legal framework for AI in New Zealand; Police use the New Technology Framework and Algorithm Charter.
Keep a human in the loop given performance inaccuracies and automation bias.
Ensure effective integration, governance and data architecture.
Align with privacy principles and Privacy Commissioner expectations, including for biometrics.
Address internal trust, deskilling and job-loss fears through open communication.
